Coming from Stata

Source: vignettes/articles/coming-from-stata.Rmd
coming-from-stata.Rmd

中文版

If you know Stata, you already know what you want to do; the question is how to say it in R. This page lists Stata commands next to the R code that does the same job, using tidystata where it has a Stata-style function and the standard package everywhere else.

Look it up from the console

findit() searches the same list from R. Type one Stata word bare, or quote anything longer. Stata’s abbreviations work.

findit(reg)
#> # Stata to R: 6 entries
#> 
#> regress y x1 x2                   # Linear regression [stats]
#>   fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data)
#> regress y x1 x2, robust           # Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors [fixest]
#>   fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero")
#> regress y x1 x2, vce(cluster id)  # Clustered standard errors [fixest]
#>   fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, cluster = ~id)
#> regress y i.group c.x1##c.x2      # Factor variables and interactions [stats]
#>   lm(y ~ factor(group) + x1 * x2, data = data)
#> regress y x [pweight = wt]        # Regression with sampling weights [fixest]
#>   fixest::feols(y ~ x, data = data, weights = ~wt, vcov = "hetero")
#> regress y ib3.group               # Choose the base category [stats]
#>   lm(y ~ relevel(factor(group), ref = "3"), data = data)
findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)")
#> # Stata to R: 10 entries
#> # "merge" is a Stata command and an R function.
#> 
#> ## Stata command
#> merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match)                            # Keep matched rows only [dplyr]
#>   inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) keepusing(id) nogenerate   # Keep rows of data1 whose id is in data2 [dplyr]
#>   semi_join(data1, data2, by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 id using data2                                         # Merge with a match report [tidystata]
#>   s_merge(data1, data2, "1:1", by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master match)                     # Keep all rows of the master data [dplyr]
#>   left_join(data1, data2, by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(using match)                      # Keep all rows of the using data [dplyr]
#>   right_join(data1, data2, by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 id1 id2 using data2, nogenerate                        # Merge on two keys [dplyr]
#>   full_join(data1, data2, by = c("id1", "id2"))
#> merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master) keepusing(id) nogenerate  # Keep rows of data1 whose id is not in data2 [dplyr]
#>   anti_join(data1, data2, by = "id")
#> merge m:1 id using data2                                         # Many-to-one merge with a match report [tidystata]
#>   s_merge(data1, data2, "m:1", by = "id")
#> merge 1:m id using data2                                         # One-to-many merge with a match report [tidystata]
#>   s_merge(data1, data2, "1:m", by = "id")
#> merge 1:1 _n using data2                                         # Put two datasets side by side by row position [dplyr]
#>   bind_cols(data1, data2)
#> 
#> ## R function: merge() [base]: Merge two data frames (base R)
#>   Related Stata: merge

Call findit() with no argument for the whole list, or ??stata to find this help again.

Where to find the rest

tidystata covers the everyday loop of inspecting, tabulating, summarising, preparing and checking data. For everything else, these packages are the usual choices:

  • Regression and fixed effects (regress, reghdfe, xtreg, ivregress): lm() and glm(), or fixest::feols().
  • Regression tables (esttab, outreg2): modelsummary::modelsummary().
  • Marginal effects (margins): marginaleffects.
  • Reshaping (reshape): tidyr::pivot_longer() and pivot_wider().
  • Winsorising (winsor2): datawizard::winsorize().
  • Panels and calendar periods (tsset, xtset, L., mofd()): tsibble and lubridate.
  • Survey data (svyset, svy:): srvyr and survey.
  • Graphs (twoway, histogram): ggplot2; for binscatter, binsreg or statar::stat_binmean().

tidystata and statar can be attached together; only tab() and xtile() share names. Attach tidystata last, or write tidystata::tab().

A few RStudio habits replace Stata’s interface: Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Return on a Mac) runs the current line or selection, Tab completes names, and the Environment and Files panes play the roles of Stata’s Variables window and dir.

In the tables below, data is your dataset, data1 and data2 are the master and using data of a merge, and fit is a fitted model. Most entries use dplyr, so attach it with library(dplyr) or library(tidyverse).

Basics

Stata R Notes
findit command findit(command) Find the R equivalent of a Stata command
Type one Stata word bare, as in findit(reg), and quote anything longer, as in findit("merge 1:1 id"). Stata abbreviations work. findit() with no argument returns the whole list.
help command help(function_name) Open the help page of a function
?function does the same. In RStudio you can also search the Help pane.
search keyword help.search("keyword") Search all installed help pages
??keyword is a shortcut. To find the R version of a Stata command, use findit().
clear rm(data) Remove a dataset from memory
Rarely needed: R holds many tables at once, each under its own name.
pwd getwd() Show the working directory
cd "path/to/folder" setwd("path/to/folder") Change the working directory
An RStudio project sets the working directory for you, so scripts can use relative paths.
dir dir() List the files in the working directory
global path "path/to/folder" path <- "path/to/folder" Store a value for later use
Any R object works like a macro: assign it once and reuse its name, as in setwd(path).
display 2 + 2 2 + 2 Calculate and show a result
ssc install package install.packages("package") Install a package
Unlike Stata, an installed package must be attached in every session with library(package).
net install package, from(url) remotes::install_github("user/package") Install a package from GitHub
do analysis.do source("analysis.R") Run a script file
log using results.log sink("results.log") Record console output in a file
Most R users write an R Markdown or Quarto report instead of a log.
sysuse auto data("mtcars") Load an example dataset
use data.dta data <- haven::read_dta("data.dta") Open a Stata dataset
Variable and value labels are kept. Data saved in R's own format open with readRDS("data.rds") or load("data.RData").
save data.dta, replace haven::write_dta(data, "data.dta") Save as a Stata dataset
saveRDS(data, "data.rds") keeps every R type, such as factors and dates, exactly.
import delimited data.csv data <- readr::read_csv("data.csv") Import a CSV file
RStudio's File > Import Dataset menu writes this code for you.
import excel data.xlsx, firstrow data <- readxl::read_excel("data.xlsx") Import an Excel sheet
import spss data.sav data <- haven::read_sav("data.sav") Import an SPSS file
export delimited data.csv readr::write_csv(data, "data.csv") Export a CSV file
export excel data.xlsx writexl::write_xlsx(data, "data.xlsx") Export an Excel file
webuse nlswork data <- haven::read_dta("https://www.stata-press.com/data/r18/nlswork.dta") Load an example dataset from the Stata website
import sas data.sas7bdat data <- haven::read_sas("data.sas7bdat") Import a SAS file
saveold data.dta, version(13) haven::write_dta(data, "data.dta", version = 13) Save for an older Stata version

Explore data

Stata R Notes
browse browse(data) View the data in a spreadsheet window
browse x1 x3-x5 browse(data, x1, x3:x5) View selected variables
Ranges of variables use a colon (x3:x5), not a dash.
browse x* y* browse(data, varlist("x* y*")) View variables matching Stata wildcards
varlist() understands Stata's * and ? wildcards and works in any selection, such as select().
browse x* select(data, starts_with("x")) Variables whose names start with given text
browse *x select(data, ends_with("x")) Variables whose names end with given text
browse *x* select(data, contains("x")) Variables whose names contain given text
browse in 1/10 head(data, 10) The first rows
browse in 7/12 slice(data, 7:12) Rows by position
browse in -10/-1 tail(data, 10) The last rows
browse if x1 == 1 & x2 == 2 filter(data, x1 == 1 & x2 == 2) Rows meeting a condition
list print_all(data) Print the first and last rows
Prints every row and column. Typing data prints the first rows; print_headtail(data) prints the first and last rows.
list x pull(data, x) Print one variable
data$x does the same. select(data, x) keeps x as a one-column table.
describe variables(data) List variables with their types and labels
glimpse(data) gives a compact view with the first values of each variable.
ds ds(data) List variable names
ds_as_column(data) returns the names as a one-column table; names(data) is base R.
codebook codebook(data) Describe every variable
lookfor income variables_search(data, "income") Find variables by name or label
tabulate x tab(data, x) One-way frequency table
fre x fre(data, x) Frequency table with totals
Like Ben Jann's fre: tab() with a total row.
tabulate x1 x2 tab2(data, x1, x2) Two-way cross-tabulation
fre2(data, x1, x2) adds row and column totals.
tabulate x [fweight = n] tab(data, x, .wt = n) Frequencies with frequency weights
tabulate x [aweight = w] tab(data, x, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic") Frequencies with analytic (sampling) weights
tab1 x1 x2 x3 tab1(data, x1, x2, x3) One frequency table per variable
tab2 x1 x2 tab2(data, x1, x2) Cross-tabulation of two variables
With three or more variables, tab2(data, x1, x2, x3) returns every pairwise table, as Stata does.
table x1 x2 x3 tab(data, x1, x2, x3) Joint frequencies of several variables
summarize summ(data) Summary statistics for all variables
summary(data) is the base R version, with a less tidy layout.
summarize x summ(data, x) Summary statistics for one variable
summarize x, detail summ(data, x, .detail = TRUE) Detailed statistics, including percentiles
Pick single statistics with .stat, as in summ(data, x, .stat = "p25").
bysort group: summarize x summ(data, x, .by = group) Summary statistics by group
group_by(data, group) |> summ(x) gives the same result.
summarize x [aweight = w] summ(data, x, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic") Weighted summary statistics
Frequency weights are the default: summ(data, x, .wt = w).
tabstat x1 x2, by(group) stat(mean sd) tabstat(data, x1, x2, .by = group, .stat = c("mean", "sd")) Chosen statistics by group
correlate x1 x2 x3 cor(select(data, x1, x2, x3), use = "complete.obs") Correlation matrix (complete cases)
pwcorr x1 x2 x3 pwcorr(data, x1, x2, x3) Pairwise correlations
Gives r, n and p for each pair; .wide = TRUE gives the matrix. Base R: cor(select(data, x1, x2, x3), use = "pairwise.complete.obs").
ttest x, by(group) t.test(x ~ group, data = data) Two-sample t test
R's default is Welch's test; add var.equal = TRUE for Stata's default equal-variance test.
tabulate x1 x2, chi2 tab2(data, x1, x2, .chi2 = TRUE) Chi-square test of independence
Also reports Cramer's V, like Stata's V option. Base R: chisq.test(data$x1, data$x2, correct = FALSE).
inspect x summ(data, x, .detail = TRUE) Distribution, zeros and missing values of a variable
hist(data$x) adds the quick histogram that inspect draws.
levelsof x sort(unique(data$x)) Distinct values of a variable
Store them for a loop: levels <- sort(unique(data$x)), then for (v in levels) { ... }.
codebook, compact summ(data) One line of statistics per variable
describe using data.dta haven::read_dta("data.dta", n_max = 0) Variables in a file, without loading its data
tabulate x, missing tab(data, x) Frequencies including missing values
tab() always lists missing values as a separate row.
tabulate x, summarize(y) summ(data, y, .by = x) Summary of y within each category of x
bysort g: tabulate x tab(data, x, .by = g) Frequency table by group
tabulate x1 x2, exact fisher.test(data$x1, data$x2) Fisher's exact test
table x, statistic(mean y) summ(data, y, .by = x, .stat = "mean") A statistic by category (Stata 17+ table)
dtable x1 x2, by(group) gtsummary::tbl_summary(data, by = group, include = c(x1, x2)) Descriptive Table 1 (Stata 18+)
modelsummary::datasummary_skim(data) gives a quick overview without a by variable.
mean x summ(data, x, .stat = c("mean", "se")) Mean with its standard error
t.test(data$x) also reports the confidence interval.
ci mean x t.test(data$x)$conf.int Confidence interval of a mean
Add conf.level = 0.99 for ci mean x, level(99).
proportion x prop.table(table(data$x)) Proportion in each category
tab(data, x) shows the same percentages; prop.test() adds a confidence interval for one proportion.
prtest x == 0.5 prop.test(sum(data$x == 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(data$x)), p = 0.5, correct = FALSE) Test of a proportion
correct = FALSE gives Stata's normal-approximation test without continuity correction.
ranksum x, by(group) wilcox.test(x ~ group, data = data) Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test
signrank x = y wilcox.test(data$x, data$y, paired = TRUE) Wilcoxon signed-rank test
kwallis x, by(group) kruskal.test(x ~ group, data = data) Kruskal-Wallis test
ksmirnov x, by(group) ks.test(data$x[data$group == 0], data$x[data$group == 1]) Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of equal distributions
anova y group summary(aov(y ~ factor(group), data = data)) Analysis of variance
oneway y group summary(aov(y ~ factor(group), data = data)) One-way analysis of variance
bartlett.test(y ~ group, data = data) gives the equal-variance test that oneway reports.
swilk x shapiro.test(data$x) Shapiro-Wilk normality test
sktest x summ(data, x, .stat = c("skew", "kurtosis")) Skewness and kurtosis
For a formal normality test use shapiro.test(data$x).
spearman x y cor.test(data$x, data$y, method = "spearman") Spearman rank correlation
ktau x y cor.test(data$x, data$y, method = "kendall") Kendall's tau
pca x1 x2 x3 prcomp(na.omit(select(data, x1, x2, x3)), scale. = TRUE) Principal components
Stata analyses the correlation matrix, so scale. = TRUE matches it.
factor x1 x2 x3 factanal(na.omit(select(data, x1, x2, x3)), factors = 1) Factor analysis
factanal() uses maximum likelihood; psych::fa(..., fm = "pa") gives Stata's default principal-factor method.
stem x stem(data$x) Stem-and-leaf display
univar x1 x2 summ(data, x1, x2, .detail = TRUE) Detailed univariate statistics

Check data

Stata R Notes
count nrow(data) Number of rows
count if x > 0 sum(data$x > 0, na.rm = TRUE) Count rows meeting a condition
isid id wave isid(data, id, wave) Check that variables identify the rows
duplicates report x1 x2 duplicates_report(data, x1, x2) Count duplicated rows
duplicates tag x1 x2, generate(dup) duplicates_tag(data, x1, x2, .name = "dup") Mark duplicated rows
duplicates list x1 x2 duplicates_list(data, x1, x2) List duplicated rows
distinct x1 x2, joint nrow(distinct(data, x1, x2)) Number of distinct combinations
misstable summarize misstable(data) Missing values per variable
Base R: colSums(is.na(data)).
misstable patterns misstable(data, .patterns = TRUE) Missing-value patterns
1 marks an observed value and 0 a missing one, as in Stata.
assert x > 0 assert(data, x > 0) Stop when a condition fails
Reports the number of contradictions and returns the data, so it fits in a pipe. Missing x counts as a contradiction, unlike Stata, where missing is larger than any number: write assert(data, is.na(x) | x > 0) for Stata's behaviour.
mdesc summ(data, .stat = "missing") Missing values per variable
confirm variable x stopifnot("x" %in% names(data)) Check that a variable exists

Labels

Stata R Notes
label define gender 1 "male" 2 "female" mutate(data, gender = factor(gender, levels = 1:2, labels = c("male", "female"))) Label every value of a categorical variable
In R a labelled categorical variable is usually a factor. Give levels explicitly so each code gets the right label.
label define x 9 "Unknown" 10 "Refused" mutate(data, x = haven::labelled(x, c(Unknown = 9, Refused = 10))) Label some values only
Partial value labels are rare in R; haven keeps them so they survive a round trip to Stata. tab() and codebook() show them.
label variable x "Variable name" labelled::set_variable_labels(data, x = "Variable name") Label a variable
Labels read from Stata files are kept; variables() and codebook() display them.
label list x levels(data$x) Show the categories of a variable
For labelled data read with haven, use haven::print_labels(data$x).
encode str_x, generate(x) mutate(data, x = factor(str_x)) Turn text into labelled categories
decode x, generate(str_x) mutate(data, str_x = decode(x)) Turn labelled values into text
label values x yesno mutate(data, x = haven::labelled(x, yesno)) Attach a value label to a variable
Define the labels once, as yesno <- c(No = 0, Yes = 1), then attach them to any variable; factor() is the usual R alternative.
label drop yesno mutate(data, x = haven::zap_labels(x)) Remove value labels
notes x: Collected in wave 2 attr(data$x, "note") <- "Collected in wave 2" Attach a note to a variable
R has no notes system; an attribute or a comment in the script is the usual substitute.

Construct and modify variables

Stata R Notes
generate x2 = x^2 mutate(data, x2 = x^2) Create a variable
Assign the result to keep it: data <- mutate(data, ...). R has no separate generate and replace.
generate n = _n mutate(data, n = row_number()) Row number
generate N = _N mutate(data, N = n()) Number of rows
Add .by = group for the number of rows in each group, like bysort group: generate N = _N.
generate x2 = x^2 if x > 0 mutate(data, x2 = if_else(x > 0, x^2, NA)) Create a variable under a condition
In Stata missing is larger than any number, so x > 0 is true for missing x. In R the condition is NA and so is the result.
generate x2 = x^2 in 11/20 mutate(data, x2 = if_else(row_number() %in% 11:20, x^2, NA)) Create a variable for some rows
generate dummy = (x1 == 1 & x2 == 2) mutate(data, dummy = as.integer(x1 == 1 & x2 == 2)) Dummy variable from a condition
Without as.integer() the result is TRUE/FALSE, which R models also accept.
generate lag_x = x[_n-1] mutate(data, lag_x = lag(x)) Value from the previous row
This shifts rows, like x[_n-1], and ignores gaps in time. See L. for panel lags.
generate lead_x = x[_n+2] mutate(data, lead_x = lead(x, 2)) Value from two rows ahead
clonevar x2 = x mutate(data, x2 = x) Copy a variable
replace x = x^2 mutate(data, x = x^2) Change a variable
replace x = x^2 if x > 0 mutate(data, x = if_else(x > 0, x^2, x)) Change a variable under a condition
replace x = x^2 in 11/20 mutate(data, x = if_else(row_number() %in% 11:20, x^2, x)) Change a variable for some rows
tabulate x, generate(x_) as_dummy(data, x) Dummy variables for every category
as_dummy(data, x, .names = "index") numbers the columns x_1, x_2, ... as Stata does. Also: fastDummies::dummy_cols(data, "x").
recode x (1/5 = 1) (6/10 = 2) (11/15 = 3) (else = .), generate(x3g) mutate(data, x3g = case_when(between(x, 1, 5) ~ 1, between(x, 6, 10) ~ 2, between(x, 11, 15) ~ 3)) Recode ranges of values
Values that match no condition become NA, like else = . in Stata.
recode x (9 = .) mutate(data, x = na_if(x, 9)) Turn one code into missing
mvdecode x, mv(-9) mutate(data, x = mvdecode(x, -9)) Turn missing-value codes into missing
mvdecode(x, c(-8, -9)) handles several codes, like mv(-8 -9).
mvencode x, mv(-9) mutate(data, x = mvencode(x, -9)) Turn missing values into a code
destring str_x, generate(num_x) mutate(data, num_x = destring(str_x)) Text to numbers
tostring num_x, generate(str_x) mutate(data, str_x = tostring(num_x)) Numbers to text
Labelled values keep their codes; decode() gives the value labels instead.
xtile q = x, nquantiles(4) mutate(data, q = xtile(x, 4)) Quantile groups
xtile() follows Stata's rule, so equal values stay in the same group.
xtile q = x [aweight = w], nquantiles(4) mutate(data, q = xtile(x, 4, wt = w)) Weighted quantile groups
egen bins = cut(x), group(10) mutate(data, bins = xtile(x, 10)) Ten groups of about equal size
egen bins = cut(x), at(0(10)100) mutate(data, bins = cut(x, breaks = seq(0, 100, 10), right = FALSE)) Groups by given cutpoints
right = FALSE makes each interval include its lower cutpoint, as egen cut() does. cut_length(x, 10) instead splits the range into 10 equal widths.
egen x_sum = rowtotal(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_sum = row_sum(x1:x5)) Row total
egen x_avg = rowmean(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_avg = row_mean(x1:x5)) Row mean
egen x_min = rowmin(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_min = row_min(x1:x5)) Row minimum
egen x_max = rowmax(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_max = row_max(x1:x5)) Row maximum
egen x_med = rowmedian(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_med = row_median(x1:x5)) Row median
egen x_sd = rowsd(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_sd = row_sd(x1:x5)) Row standard deviation
egen x_mi = rowmiss(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_mi = row_miss(x1:x5)) Number of missing values in each row
egen x_n = rownonmiss(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_n = row_non_miss(x1:x5)) Number of observed values in each row
egen x_nv = rownvals(x1-x5) mutate(data, x_nv = row_nvals(x1:x5)) Number of distinct values in each row
From egenmore (SSC). Missing values are ignored unless .missing = TRUE, like the missing option.
egen x_avg = mean(x) mutate(data, x_avg = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) Sample statistic as a new variable
R functions keep missing values unless na.rm = TRUE; Stata's egen ignores them.
bysort group: egen x_avg = mean(x) mutate(data, x_avg = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group statistic as a new variable
egen id = group(g1 g2) data |> group_by(g1, g2) |> mutate(id = cur_group_id()) |> ungroup() Number the groups
egen first = tag(group) mutate(data, first = is_first(group)) Mark the first row of each group
Gives TRUE/FALSE; rows with a missing group are FALSE, as in Stata, unless .missing = TRUE.
egen z = std(x) mutate(data, z = std(x)) Standardise a variable
Base R: as.vector(scale(x)). Add .by = g for by g: egen.
egen p = pc(x) mutate(data, p = pc(x)) Percentage of the total
pc(x, prop = TRUE) gives proportions, like the prop option.
winsor2 x, cuts(1 99) mutate(data, x_w = datawizard::winsorize(x, threshold = 0.01)) Winsorise at the 1st and 99th percentiles
rename x x2 rename(data, x2 = x) Rename a variable
Note the order: new name = old name.
rename *, lower rename_with(data, tolower) Make all names lower case
collapse (mean) x1 x2, by(group) summarise(data, across(c(x1, x2), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .by = group) Replace the data with group means
Assign the result to replace the data, as collapse does: data <- summarise(...). summ(data, x1, x2, .by = group) shows a summary table instead.
collapse (count) n = x (sum) total = y, by(group) summarise(data, n = sum(!is.na(x)), total = sum(y, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Different statistics for different variables
egen r = rank(x) mutate(data, r = rank(x, na.last = "keep")) Rank, with ties averaged
rank() gives tied values their average rank, like egen rank(); dplyr::min_rank() gives them the lowest.
bysort group: egen tot = total(x) mutate(data, tot = sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group total
bysort group: egen n = count(x) mutate(data, n = sum(!is.na(x)), .by = group) Number of observed values in each group
bysort group: egen mx = max(x) mutate(data, mx = max(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group maximum
For a group with only missing values R returns -Inf with a warning; Stata returns missing.
bysort group: egen mn = min(x) mutate(data, mn = min(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group minimum
bysort group: egen s = sd(x) mutate(data, s = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group standard deviation
bysort group: egen med = median(x) mutate(data, med = median(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group) Group median
egen id = concat(a b), punct(_) mutate(data, id = paste(a, b, sep = "_")) Join variables into one string
egen n9 = anycount(x1-x5), values(9) mutate(data, n9 = rowSums(across(x1:x5, ~ .x %in% 9))) Count how many variables equal a value
egen first = rowfirst(x1-x5) mutate(data, first = coalesce(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5)) First observed value across variables
egen last = rowlast(x1-x5) mutate(data, last = coalesce(x5, x4, x3, x2, x1)) Last observed value across variables
egen s = seq(), from(1) to(3) mutate(data, s = rep_len(1:3, n())) Repeating sequence
pctile p = x, nquantiles(4) quantile(data$x, probs = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE, type = 2) Quantile cutpoints
type = 2 averages at exact positions, like Stata's default percentile definition; R's default is type 7.
generate y = cond(x > 0, 1, 0) mutate(data, y = if_else(x > 0, 1, 0)) One value if a condition holds, another if not
With missing x, Stata's cond() takes the first value (missing counts as large); if_else() returns NA.
generate y = inlist(x, 1, 3, 5) mutate(data, y = x %in% c(1, 3, 5)) Whether x equals any listed value
%in% gives FALSE for missing x, as inlist() does.
generate y = inrange(x, 1, 5) mutate(data, y = between(x, 1, 5)) Whether x lies within a range
between() returns NA for missing x, whereas Stata's inrange() returns 0.
generate m = missing(x) mutate(data, m = is.na(x)) Whether a value is missing
generate y = round(x, 0.1) mutate(data, y = round(x, 1)) Round
R's second argument is the number of decimals. R rounds halves to even (round(0.5) is 0); Stata rounds them up.
generate y = floor(x) mutate(data, y = floor(x)) Round down
generate y = ceil(x) mutate(data, y = ceiling(x)) Round up
generate y = ln(x) mutate(data, y = log(x)) Natural logarithm
log10() matches Stata's log10(). R's log(0) is -Inf rather than missing.
generate u = runiform() mutate(data, u = runif(n())) Uniform random numbers
generate z = rnormal() mutate(data, z = rnorm(n())) Normal random numbers
generate cs = sum(x) mutate(data, cs = cumsum(coalesce(x, 0))) Running sum
Stata's sum() function treats missing values as 0, hence coalesce(x, 0).
generate days = d2 - d1 mutate(data, days = as.numeric(d2 - d1)) Days between two dates
recast double x mutate(data, x = as.double(x)) Change the storage type
R chooses storage automatically, so there is no compress either.
format x %9.2f mutate(data, x_text = sprintf("%.2f", x)) Display numbers with two decimals
R stores the number unchanged and formats it only when printing, for example with round(x, 2) or sprintf().
rename (a b) (c d) rename(data, c = a, d = b) Rename several variables
rename x*, upper rename_with(data, toupper, starts_with("x")) Upper-case some names
rename * *_old rename_with(data, ~ paste0(.x, "_old")) Add a suffix to every name

Select variables and rows

Stata R Notes
keep x1 x3-x5 select(data, x1, x3:x5) Keep some variables
Numbers select by position: select(data, 1, 3:5). s_select() also computes new columns.
keep x* select(data, varlist("x*")) Keep variables matching Stata wildcards
drop x select(data, -x) Drop a variable
drop x1 x3-x5 select(data, -c(x1, x3:x5)) Drop several variables
Positions work too: select(data, -c(1, 3:5)).
keep in 1/10 head(data, 10) Keep the first rows
keep in 7/12 slice(data, 7:12) Keep rows by position
keep in -10/-1 tail(data, 10) Keep the last rows
keep if x1 == 1 & x2 == 2 filter(data, x1 == 1 & x2 == 2) Keep rows meeting a condition
filter() drops rows where the condition is NA, so rows with missing values never pass.
keep if !missing(x) filter(data, !is.na(x)) Keep rows where x is observed
drop if x == 1 filter(data, x != 1 | is.na(x)) Drop rows meeting a condition
Stata keeps rows with missing x here; | is.na(x) does the same in R.
duplicates drop duplicates_drop(data) Drop rows that duplicate an earlier row
duplicates drop x1 x2, force duplicates_drop(data, x1, x2, .force = TRUE) Keep the first row for each key
distinct(data, x1, x2, .keep_all = TRUE) is the dplyr version.
set seed 2024; sample 1000, count data |> slice_sample(n = 1000) |> set_seed(2024) Reproducible random sample of 1000 rows
set_seed() sets the seed before the sampling step runs, so the pipe stays in one line.
set seed 2024; sample 10 data |> slice_sample(prop = 0.1) |> set_seed(2024) Reproducible random 10% sample
drop in 1/4 slice(data, -(1:4)) Drop rows by position
drop if missing(x) filter(data, !is.na(x)) Drop rows where x is missing
keep if inlist(x, 1, 3, 5) filter(data, x %in% c(1, 3, 5)) Keep rows with listed values
keep if inrange(x, 5000, 10000) filter(data, between(x, 5000, 10000)) Keep rows within a range

Sort

Stata R Notes
order x1-x4 relocate(data, x1:x4) Move variables to the front
order x1-x4, before(x5) relocate(data, x1:x4, .before = x5) Move variables before another
sort x1 x2 arrange(data, x1, x2) Sort in ascending order
gsort x1 -x2 arrange(data, x1, desc(x2)) Sort ascending and descending

Combine data

Stata R Notes
append using data2 bind_rows(data1, data2) Stack two datasets
merge 1:1 id using data2 s_merge(data1, data2, "1:1", by = "id") Merge with a match report
Like Stata, all rows are kept and a .merge column records the match result. full_join(data1, data2, by = "id") merges without the report.
merge m:1 id using data2 s_merge(data1, data2, "m:1", by = "id") Many-to-one merge with a match report
merge 1:m id using data2 s_merge(data1, data2, "1:m", by = "id") One-to-many merge with a match report
merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id") Keep matched rows only
merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master match) left_join(data1, data2, by = "id") Keep all rows of the master data
merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(using match) right_join(data1, data2, by = "id") Keep all rows of the using data
merge 1:1 id1 id2 using data2, nogenerate full_join(data1, data2, by = c("id1", "id2")) Merge on two keys
Variables with the same name in both tables get suffixes; choose them with suffix = c("_data1", "_data2").
merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) keepusing(id) nogenerate semi_join(data1, data2, by = "id") Keep rows of data1 whose id is in data2
merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master) keepusing(id) nogenerate anti_join(data1, data2, by = "id") Keep rows of data1 whose id is not in data2
merge 1:1 _n using data2 bind_cols(data1, data2) Put two datasets side by side by row position
joinby id using data2 inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id", relationship = "many-to-many") All pairs of rows within each id
append using data2, generate(source) bind_rows(data1, data2, .id = "source") Stack datasets and record where each row came from
cross using data2 cross_join(data1, data2) Every combination of rows from two datasets

Reshape

Stata R Notes
reshape long var, i(id) j(year) pivot_longer(data, starts_with("var"), names_to = "year", names_prefix = "var", values_to = "var") Wide to long
year comes back as text; add names_transform = list(year = as.integer) for numbers. pivot_longer(data, -id) stacks every other variable whatever its name.
reshape wide var, i(id) j(year) pivot_wider(data, names_from = year, values_from = var, names_prefix = "var") Long to wide
xpose, clear tibble::as_tibble(t(data), .name_repair = "unique") Transpose the data

Construct data

Stata R Notes
input x y tibble(x = c(1, 2), y = c(3, 4)) Type in a small dataset
fillin x1 x2 complete(data, x1, x2) Add rows for every combination of values
expand(data, x1, x2) returns only the combinations; expand_grid(x1 = 1:5, x2 = c("a", "b")) builds them from scratch.
expand n uncount(data, n) Repeat each row n times
uncount() drops n afterwards; add .remove = FALSE to keep it.
set obs 100 data <- tibble(id = 1:100) Start a dataset with a given number of rows

Strings and dates

Stata R Notes
split name, parse(" ") separate_wider_delim(data, name, delim = " ", names_sep = "_", too_few = "align_start") Split text into several variables
generate s = substr(name, 1, 3) mutate(data, s = str_sub(name, 1, 3)) Part of a string
generate n = strlen(name) mutate(data, n = str_length(name)) Length of a string
generate s = upper(name) mutate(data, s = str_to_upper(name)) Upper case
generate s = lower(name) mutate(data, s = str_to_lower(name)) Lower case
generate s = strtrim(name) mutate(data, s = str_trim(name)) Remove leading and trailing spaces
generate s = subinstr(name, "a", "b", .) mutate(data, s = str_replace_all(name, fixed("a"), "b")) Replace text
stringr treats patterns as regular expressions; fixed() matches the text literally, as subinstr() does.
generate has = strpos(name, "a") > 0 mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, fixed("a"))) Whether a string contains some text
generate has = regexm(name, "^A") mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, "^A")) Match a regular expression
generate d = date(s, "YMD") mutate(data, d = lubridate::ymd(s)) Text to a date
generate d = mdy(m, d, y) mutate(data, d = lubridate::make_date(y, m, d)) Date from year, month and day
generate y = year(d) mutate(data, y = lubridate::year(d)) Year of a date
lubridate::month(), day() and wday() extract the other parts.
generate m = mofd(d) mutate(data, m = tsibble::yearmonth(d)) Monthly period from a date
tsibble::yearquarter() is the quarterly version, like qofd().
generate w = word(name, 1) mutate(data, w = stringr::word(name, 1)) The first word of a string
generate n = wordcount(name) mutate(data, n = str_count(name, "\\S+")) Number of words
generate m = strmatch(name, "A*") mutate(data, m = grepl(glob2rx("A*"), name)) Match a wildcard pattern
generate s = regexr(name, "[0-9]+", "") mutate(data, s = str_replace(name, "[0-9]+", "")) Replace the first regular-expression match
str_replace_all() replaces every match, like ustrregexra().
generate d = regexs(1) if regexm(name, "([0-9]+)") mutate(data, d = str_extract(name, "[0-9]+")) Extract the matching text
generate has = ustrregexm(name, "^a", 1) mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, regex("^a", ignore_case = TRUE))) Unicode-aware regular expression, ignoring case
stringr is Unicode-aware throughout, so the u- forms of Stata's string functions need no special version.
generate s = stritrim(name) mutate(data, s = str_squish(name)) Collapse repeated spaces
str_squish() also removes leading and trailing spaces.
generate s = strupper(name) mutate(data, s = str_to_upper(name)) Upper case
generate s = strlower(name) mutate(data, s = str_to_lower(name)) Lower case
generate s = strproper(name) mutate(data, s = str_to_title(name)) Title case
generate s = string(x) mutate(data, s = as.character(x)) Number to text
tidystata's decode() uses value labels for labelled data; tostring() keeps the codes.
generate x = real(s) mutate(data, x = as.numeric(s)) Text to a number
destring() from tidystata also strips value labels.
generate n = strtoname(s) mutate(data, n = make.names(s)) Turn text into a valid name
janitor::clean_names(data) cleans every variable name at once.
generate m = month(d) mutate(data, m = lubridate::month(d)) Month of a date
generate dd = day(d) mutate(data, dd = lubridate::day(d)) Day of the month
generate w = dow(d) mutate(data, w = lubridate::wday(d) - 1) Day of the week
wday() counts Sunday as 1; Stata's dow() counts Sunday as 0.
generate q = qofd(d) mutate(data, q = tsibble::yearquarter(d)) Quarterly period from a date
generate d = dofm(m) mutate(data, d = as.Date(m)) First day of a monthly period
Here m is a tsibble::yearmonth() value.
generate t = clock(s, "YMDhms") mutate(data, t = lubridate::ymd_hms(s)) Text to a date-time
format d %td format(data$d, "%d%b%Y") Display a date
Dates keep their class; format() only changes how they print.
display c(current_date) Sys.Date() Today's date
generate age = (d2 - d1) / 365.25 mutate(data, age = lubridate::time_length(lubridate::interval(d1, d2), "years")) Age or duration in years

Loops and programming

Stata R Notes
foreach v of varlist v1-v5 { generate `v'_sq = `v'^2 } mutate(data, across(v1:v5, ~ .x^2, .names = "{col}_sq")) Same calculation for several variables
across() replaces most variable loops; for other loops R has for (v in names) { ... }.
forvalues i = 1/5 { generate v`i'_sq = v`i'^2 if v`i' > 0 } mutate(data, across(v1:v5, ~ if_else(.x > 0, .x^2, NA), .names = "{col}_sq")) Loop with a condition
forvalues i = 6/10 { forvalues j = 3/5 { replace x_`i'_`j' = x_`i'_`j' + 1 } } mutate(data, across(matches("^x_([6-9]|10)_[3-5]$"), ~ .x + 1)) Loop over variables numbered in their names
A regular expression picks the names. varlist("x_[6-10]_*") works when only one number range is needed.
capture command capture(expression) Run code and report success instead of stopping
capture() returns TRUE or FALSE. Use try() to keep the error message.
quietly regress y x fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = data) Run without printing
Assigning a result never prints it; print(fit) or summary(fit) shows it later.
timer on 1 timer(expression) Time how long code takes
set seed 2024 set.seed(2024) Make random numbers reproducible
set_seed(.fn, seed) sets the seed inside a pipe; see the sample rows.
preserve backup <- data Keep a copy to return to
R never changes data in place, so keep the original object and assign results to a new name; restore is data <- backup.
local vars x1 x2 x3 vars <- c("x1", "x2", "x3") Store a list of variable names
Use it with all_of(): select(data, all_of(vars)) or across(all_of(vars), ...).
scalar a = 3 a <- 3 Store a single number
matrix A = (1, 2 \ 3, 4) A <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE) Create a matrix
return list str(summ(data, x)) See the results a command stored
R results are ordinary objects: assign them and pick out parts, as in s <- summ(data, x); s$mean.
ereturn list broom::glance(fit) Model statistics
broom::tidy(fit) gives the coefficient table, and names(fit) lists every stored part.
display _b[x] coef(fit)["x"] A stored coefficient
display _se[x] sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))["x"] A stored standard error
while `i' < 10 { local i = `i' + 1 } while (i < 10) { i <- i + 1 } Repeat while a condition holds
if `x' > 0 { display "positive" } if (x > 0) print("positive") Run code only if a condition holds
Quote it: findit("if"), because if is a reserved word in R.
program define myprog myprog <- function(data) { summ(data) } Write your own command
tempfile f f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") A temporary file
Temporary variables are not needed: intermediate columns can be dropped, or kept as separate objects.
set trace on traceback() Find where an error happened
debug(f) or browser() steps through a function line by line.
clear all rm(list = ls()) Remove every object
Restarting R (Session > Restart R in RStudio) gives a truly clean start.
frame create other other <- tibble() Hold another dataset
R keeps any number of data frames as separate objects, so frames are built in.
which summarize getAnywhere("summ") Where a command comes from
ado update update.packages() Update installed packages
version 18 R.version.string Version control
renv::snapshot() records package versions so a project can be reproduced later.
cls cat("\014") Clear the console
In RStudio, Ctrl+L does the same.
macro list ls() List defined objects

Models and tables

Stata R Notes
regress y x1 x2 fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data) Linear regression
summary(fit) shows the coefficient table; broom::tidy(fit) returns it as a data frame.
regress y x1 x2, robust fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero") Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
regress y x1 x2, vce(cluster id) fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, cluster = ~id) Clustered standard errors
regress y i.group c.x1##c.x2 lm(y ~ factor(group) + x1 * x2, data = data) Factor variables and interactions
factor() plays the role of i.; x1 * x2 is c.x1##c.x2 and x1:x2 is c.x1#c.x2.
regress y x [pweight = wt] fixest::feols(y ~ x, data = data, weights = ~wt, vcov = "hetero") Regression with sampling weights
For full survey designs with strata and clusters, see svyset.
reghdfe y x, absorb(id year) fixest::feols(y ~ x | id + year, data = data) High-dimensional fixed effects
xtreg y x, fe fixest::feols(y ~ x | id, data = data) Panel fixed effects
xtreg y x, re plm::plm(y ~ x, data = data, index = c("id", "year"), model = "random") Panel random effects
ivregress 2sls y x1 (x2 = z) fixest::feols(y ~ x1 | x2 ~ z, data = data) Instrumental variables (2SLS)
logit y x1 x2 glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = binomial, data = data) Logit model
probit y x1 x2 glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = binomial(link = "probit"), data = data) Probit model
poisson y x1 x2 glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = poisson, data = data) Poisson model
margins, dydx(*) marginaleffects::avg_slopes(fit) Average marginal effects
margins group marginaleffects::avg_predictions(fit, by = "group") Predictive margins by group
predict yhat mutate(data, yhat = predict(fit, newdata = data)) Fitted values
residuals(fit) gives residuals for the rows used in the model.
test x1 = x2 marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, "x1 = x2") Test a hypothesis about coefficients
estimates store m1 m1 <- lm(y ~ x, data = data) Keep a model for later
A fitted model is an ordinary object; keep as many as you like under different names.
esttab m1 m2 modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2)) Regression table
outreg2 using table.doc modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2), output = "table.docx") Regression table in a Word file
glm y x, family(binomial) glm(y ~ x, family = binomial, data = data) Generalised linear model
logit y x, or broom::tidy(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial, data = data), exponentiate = TRUE) Odds ratios
logistic y x broom::tidy(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial, data = data), exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) Logit model reported as odds ratios
predict p, pr mutate(data, p = predict(fit, newdata = data, type = "response")) Predicted probabilities
predict r, residuals mutate(data, r = y - predict(fit, newdata = data)) Residuals for every row
regress y ib3.group lm(y ~ relevel(factor(group), ref = "3"), data = data) Choose the base category
mlogit y x1 x2 nnet::multinom(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data) Multinomial logit
ologit y x1 x2 MASS::polr(factor(y) ~ x1 + x2, data = data, Hess = TRUE) Ordered logit
Hess = TRUE lets summary() show standard errors.
oprobit y x1 x2 MASS::polr(factor(y) ~ x1 + x2, data = data, method = "probit", Hess = TRUE) Ordered probit
nbreg y x MASS::glm.nb(y ~ x, data = data) Negative binomial model
fixest::fenegbin() adds fixed effects.
ppmlhdfe y x, absorb(id year) fixest::fepois(y ~ x | id + year, data = data) Poisson model with fixed effects
tobit y x, ll(0) AER::tobit(y ~ x, left = 0, data = data) Censored (tobit) regression
qreg y x quantreg::rq(y ~ x, tau = 0.5, data = data) Median (quantile) regression
rreg y x MASS::rlm(y ~ x, data = data) Robust regression
rlm() uses Huber M-estimation; Stata's rreg combines Huber and biweight steps, so estimates can differ slightly.
areg y x, absorb(id) fixest::feols(y ~ x | id, data = data) Regression absorbing one categorical variable
xtlogit y x, fe survival::clogit(y ~ x + strata(id), data = data) Conditional (fixed-effects) logit
fixest::feglm(y ~ x | id, family = binomial) is faster but estimates unconditional fixed effects.
xtpoisson y x, fe fixest::fepois(y ~ x | id, data = data) Fixed-effects Poisson
mixed y x || id: lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = data) Multilevel (mixed) linear model
lme4 reports no p-values; lmerTest::lmer() adds them.
melogit y x || id: lme4::glmer(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = binomial) Multilevel logit
heckman y x, select(s = z) sampleSelection::selection(s ~ z, y ~ x, data = data) Heckman selection model
sem (y <- x1 x2) lavaan::sem("y ~ x1 + x2", data = data) Structural equation model
cluster kmeans x1 x2, k(3) kmeans(na.omit(select(data, x1, x2)), centers = 3) K-means clustering
bootstrap, reps(500): regress y x lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov = sandwich::vcovBS(fit, R = 500)) Bootstrap standard errors
jackknife: regress y x lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov = sandwich::vcovJK(fit)) Jackknife standard errors
lincom x1 - x2 marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, "x1 - x2 = 0") Linear combination of coefficients
nlcom _b[x1] / _b[x2] marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, "x1 / x2 = 0") Nonlinear combination of coefficients
Standard errors use the delta method, as in Stata.
lrtest m1 m2 lmtest::lrtest(m1, m2) Likelihood-ratio test
estat ic c(AIC = AIC(fit), BIC = BIC(fit)) Information criteria
estat vce vcov(fit) Variance-covariance matrix
estat hettest lmtest::bptest(fit, ~ fitted(fit), studentize = FALSE) Breusch-Pagan test for heteroskedasticity
These options match Stata's default test against the fitted values.
estat ovtest lmtest::resettest(fit, power = 2:4) RESET test for omitted variables
vif car::vif(fit) Variance inflation factors
rvfplot plot(fit, which = 1) Residuals against fitted values
avplots car::avPlots(fit) Added-variable plots
marginsplot marginaleffects::plot_predictions(fit, condition = "x") Plot predictive margins
estimates table m1 m2 modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2), output = "markdown") Compare models side by side
eststo m1: regress y x m1 <- lm(y ~ x, data = data) Store a model for a table
etable modelsummary::modelsummary(fit) Table of the last model (Stata 17+)
putexcel set results.xlsx writexl::write_xlsx(results, "results.xlsx") Write results to Excel
openxlsx2 gives cell-level control over formatting.
putdocx begin flextable::save_as_docx(flextable::flextable(results), path = "results.docx") Write a table to Word
officer builds whole Word documents.
teffects psmatch (y) (t x1 x2) MatchIt::matchit(t ~ x1 + x2, data = data, method = "nearest") Propensity-score matching
Estimate the effect on the matched data, for example lm(y ~ t, data = MatchIt::match.data(m), weights = weights).
teffects ipw (y) (t x1 x2) WeightIt::weightit(t ~ x1 + x2, data = data, method = "glm") Inverse-probability weighting
synth y x1 x2, trunit(1) trperiod(2000) Synth::synth(data.prep.obj = prep) Synthetic control
Synth::dataprep() builds prep from the panel first; tidysynth offers a tidier interface.
didregress (y) (treated), group(id) time(year) fixest::feols(y ~ treated | id + year, data = data) Difference in differences (Stata 17+)
csdid y, ivar(id) time(year) gvar(first_treat) did::att_gt(yname = "y", tname = "year", idname = "id", gname = "first_treat", data = data) Staggered difference in differences
rdrobust y x, c(0) rdrobust::rdrobust(data$y, data$x, c = 0) Regression discontinuity
ivreg2 y x1 (x2 = z), robust fixest::feols(y ~ x1 | x2 ~ z, data = data, vcov = "hetero") Instrumental variables with robust errors
fixest::fitstat(fit, ~ ivf + ivwald) reports first-stage statistics.
oaxaca y x1 x2, by(group) oaxaca::oaxaca(y ~ x1 + x2 | group, data = data) Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition
xtabond y x plm::pgmm(y ~ lag(y, 1) + x | lag(y, 2:99), data = data, index = c("id", "year")) Dynamic panel (Arellano-Bond)
mi impute chained (regress) x1 x2 = y imp <- mice::mice(data, m = 20) Multiple imputation
mi estimate: regress y x mice::pool(with(imp, lm(y ~ x))) Fit and combine models across imputations

Panel and time series

Stata R Notes
xtset id year tsibble::as_tsibble(data, key = id, index = year) Declare panel data
tidystata needs no declaration: s_lag(x, time = year) with .by = id, and fixest takes panel.id = ~id + year.
tsset year tsibble::as_tsibble(data, index = year) Declare time-series data
generate lag_x = L.x mutate(data, lag_x = s_lag(x, time = year), .by = id) Lag within each panel
Like Stata, gaps in year give missing values; dplyr::lag() shifts rows instead. Use s_lag(x, 2, time = year) for L2.x and unit = "month" for monthly dates.
generate lead_x = F.x mutate(data, lead_x = s_lead(x, time = year), .by = id) Lead within each panel
Gaps in year give missing values, as in Stata.
generate d_x = D.x mutate(data, d_x = s_diff(x, time = year), .by = id) First difference within each panel
s_diff(x, 2, time = year) is D2.x, the difference of differences.
tsfill tsibble::fill_gaps(ts_data) Add rows for missing time points
generate lag2_x = L2.x mutate(data, lag2_x = lag(x, 2, order_by = year), .by = id) Two-period lag within each panel
xtdescribe count(count(data, id, name = "periods"), periods) How many periods each panel unit has
xtsum x data |> mutate(m = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = id) |> summarise(overall = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), within = sd(x - m, na.rm = TRUE)) Overall and within standard deviations
The between part is the standard deviation of the id means: summarise(data, m = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = id) then sd(m).
tsline y ggplot(data, aes(year, y)) + geom_line() Time-series line plot
xtline y ggplot(data, aes(year, y)) + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~id) One line plot per panel unit
aes(group = id) without facets draws all units in one plot, like the overlay option.
arima y, ar(1/2) arima(data$y, order = c(2, 0, 0)) ARIMA model
carryforward x, replace tidyr::fill(data, x, .direction = "down") Carry the last observed value forward
group_by(data, id) first to fill within each panel unit.

Survival analysis

Stata R Notes
stset time, failure(died) survival::Surv(data$time, data$died) Declare survival-time data
R has no declaration step: Surv(time, died) goes on the left of each model formula.
sts graph plot(survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ 1, data = data)) Kaplan-Meier curve
sts test group survival::survdiff(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ group, data = data) Log-rank test
stsum survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ 1, data = data) Summary of survival times
stcox x1 x2 survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ x1 + x2, data = data) Cox proportional hazards model
exp(coef(fit)) gives the hazard ratios that stcox reports.
streg x, distribution(weibull) survival::survreg(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ x, data = data, dist = "weibull") Parametric survival model
survreg() reports the accelerated failure-time form; Stata's Weibull default is the hazard form, so signs and scales differ.

Survey data

Stata R Notes
svyset psu [pweight = wt], strata(stratum) design <- srvyr::as_survey_design(data, ids = psu, strata = stratum, weights = wt) Declare a survey design
svy: mean x summarise(design, x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) Survey-weighted mean
svy: tabulate x design |> group_by(x) |> summarise(p = srvyr::survey_prop()) Survey-weighted proportions
svy: regress y x survey::svyglm(y ~ x, design = design) Survey-weighted regression
svy: mean x, over(g) design |> group_by(g) |> summarise(x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) Survey-weighted means by group
svy, subpop(rural): mean x design |> filter(rural == 1) |> summarise(x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) Subpopulation estimate
Filtering a survey design keeps the full design for the variance, as subpop() does.
svy: proportion x design |> group_by(x) |> summarise(p = srvyr::survey_prop(vartype = "ci")) Survey-weighted proportions with intervals
svy: logit y x survey::svyglm(y ~ x, design = design, family = quasibinomial()) Survey-weighted logit
svydescribe summary(design) Describe the survey design

Graphs

Stata R Notes
histogram x ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_histogram() Histogram
kdensity x ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_density() Density plot
scatter y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() Scatter plot
twoway (scatter y x) (lfit y x) ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") Scatter plot with a fitted line
line y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_line() Line plot
graph bar (mean) y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar") Bar chart of group means
graph box y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + geom_boxplot() Box plot
graph export figure.png ggsave("figure.png") Save the last graph
binscatter y x binsreg::binsreg(y, x, data = data) Binned scatter plot
statar::stat_binmean() adds binned means to a ggplot: ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + statar::stat_binmean(n = 20).
coefplot modelsummary::modelplot(fit) Coefficient plot
graph bar (count), over(x) ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_bar() Bar chart of counts
graph hbar (mean) y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar") + coord_flip() Horizontal bar chart
graph dot (mean) y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(y, group)) + stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point") Dot chart
graph hbox y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(y, group)) + geom_boxplot() Horizontal box plot
graph pie, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(x = "", fill = group)) + geom_bar() + coord_polar(theta = "y") Pie chart
graph matrix x1 x2 x3 pairs(select(data, x1, x2, x3)) Scatter-plot matrix
GGally::ggpairs() draws a ggplot2 version.
graph combine g1.gph g2.gph patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2) Combine plots
With patchwork attached, p1 + p2 does the same.
graph save fig.gph saveRDS(p, "fig.rds") Save a plot to edit later
twoway connected y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_line() + geom_point() Connected line plot
twoway area y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_area() Area plot
twoway lfitci y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_smooth(method = "lm") Linear fit with a confidence band
twoway qfit y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE) Quadratic fit
twoway rcap hi lo x ggplot(data, aes(x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) + geom_errorbar() Range plot with capped spikes
twoway rarea hi lo x ggplot(data, aes(x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) + geom_ribbon() Shaded range
twoway scatter y x, by(group) ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~group) One panel per group
twoway (scatter y x if g == 1) (scatter y x if g == 2) ggplot(data, aes(x, y, colour = factor(g))) + geom_point() Colour points by group
lowess y x ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "loess") Smoothed scatter plot
scatter y x, mlabel(name) ggplot(data, aes(x, y, label = name)) + geom_point() + geom_text() Label the points
scatter y x, xline(0) ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) Add a reference line
geom_hline(yintercept = 0) is yline().
vioplot y, over(group) ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + geom_violin() Violin plot
qnorm x ggplot(data, aes(sample = x)) + geom_qq() + geom_qq_line() Normal quantile plot
set scheme s1mono theme_set(theme_bw()) Change the look of every graph
